Regal Rexnord has solved this problem with its Groove Tool, which reduces yaw
brake noise. This device cuts grooves in the yaw brake disc, which acts like a razor
as the turbine moves to meet the wind, cutting debris from the brake pad. A brush
located bet ween brakes removes the debris from the grooves, allowing the disc to
clean itself, while helping to safeguard braking performance.
This permanent solution can be adapted to meet the specific needs of any given
turbine design. Taking into account wind direction, turbine diameter and disc
material; Svendborg Brakes inputs dat a into propriet ar y computer programmes to
